sections.heading: Quick review

lines.en: The key is in the bag.

sections.note: Say each phrase aloud before you hear the English.

sections.heading: Dialogue

lines.en: Its name is Noor, and its office is in Abuja.
And you, do you have a company?

lines.ar: نَعَمْ، عِنْدِي شَرِكَةُ بَرْمَجِيَّاتٍ فِي لَاغُوسَ.
lines.en: Yes, I have a software company in Lagos.
Thanks. And this is my card.

sections.note: Listen, then read it aloud. Play both roles. At a tech event, Ridhwan meets a woman named Maryam.

sections.heading: How it works

lines.en: What's your name? Said to a man.
What's your name? Said to a woman.

sections.note: To say your to a woman, add ki instead of ka: ismuki, your name. Also, a word ending in taa marbuta turns that ending into a full t before any ending: sharika, a company, becomes sharikatee, my company.

sections.heading: Word builder: the root ain, raa, faa, meaning knowing

lines.en: well known, the thing that is known
Your company is well known. Said to a woman.

sections.note: You know faa-il, maf-al, maf-ool, fa-eel and mif-aal. Today's new pattern is tafaa-ul, an action people do with each other. Ta-aaruf means getting to know each other, exactly what happens at an event.

sections.heading: Speak it

lines.en: Model answer: Yes, I have a software company.
Model answer: My company's office is in Nigeria.
Model answer: Her name is Fatima, and she's a designer.

sections.note: Answer each question aloud about yourself. Then listen to the model answer.
